headline: 3 detained after 4 family members found dead in locked Rangpur home
summary: An ex-schoolteacher, his wife, and their two children were found dead in their residence; police suspect strangulation and robbery.
details: Police have detained three suspects, including individuals named Siddhartha and Mugdho, after four members of the same family were found dead in a locked house in Machhuapara, Rangpur city.

The deceased are Ganapati Chakraborty (65), a retired teacher of Rangpur Zilla School, his wife Pritilata Bala Chakraborty (55), their daughter Pranti (25), and their son Priyam (12), a student of class five.

The bodies were recovered during an operation from Saturday night to Sunday morning. They were found in different parts of the house: the father near the roof door, the mother and daughter under the roof stairs, and the son under a bed on the second floor.
Police suspect the victims were strangled to death, as marks of injury were found on their necks and pieces of cloth or nylon rope were wrapped around their mouths.
Investigators believe the deaths occurred three to four days ago, as the bodies had begun to decompose. The house's electricity was disconnected, and drawers were found broken, suggesting a robbery.

The incident came to light after the victims' relatives became suspicious when their phones remained switched off. Upon entering the house, they found the furniture ransacked and the main gate locked from the outside.
The Rangpur Metropolitan Police and CID are investigating the motive, focusing on the theft of money and valuables. A formal case has not yet been filed, but questioning of the detainees is ongoing.

headline_marked: Bangladesh suffer [[innings defeat in Mackay]] as Australia level series 1-1
headline: Bangladesh suffer innings defeat in Mackay as Australia level series 1-1
summary: The Tigers collapsed to 95 all out in their second innings, marking the first time in 21 years they were bowled out for under 100 twice in a single Test.
details: Australia won the Mackay Test by an innings and 51 runs after bowling Bangladesh out for 95 on Sunday. The defeat leaves the two-match series tied 1-1 after Bangladesh won the opening Test in Darwin by nine wickets.
The loss was marked by a historic batting collapse, as it was the first time in 21 years that Bangladesh was bowled out for under 100 in both innings of a single Test match.

Mitchell Starc was the standout performer for Australia, taking six wickets in the first innings and four in the second to finish with 10 wickets in the match. Captain Pat Cummins also claimed six wickets.
Bangladesh's batting struggled throughout the second innings, with Litton Das recording a hat-trick of ducks in the series. Skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto managed 31 before being caught at long-off.

Mushfiqur Rahim provided the only significant resistance in the second innings with an unbeaten 29. Shoriful Islam was the bright spot for the Tigers with the ball, taking seven wickets in Australia's first innings.
The match concluded quickly on the second day after Taskin Ahmed fell for eight and Shoriful Islam was dismissed for a duck, wrapping up the innings shortly after the tea break.
